text:
kai: quick sync  I'm leaning toward a hybrid resume design: trailers for heavy streaming checkpoints + a tiny session header fallback for legacy clients. want to capture tradeoffs and rollout steps.

maria: trailers = nice for server-side checkpoints. avoids inflating request headers on repeated retries. but many mobile SDKs and some frontdoors don't handle http trailers.

ingrid: agreed. hybrid sounds sensible. sketch: client always sends `X-RW-Session: v1|<sid>` (small uuid). server emits full checkpoint in a `Resume-Trailer: v1|base64(...)` trailer. proxies that support trailers forward it; proxies that don't persist the trailer in an encrypted edge-store keyed by sid.

kai: resume handshake example: when client reconnects or proxy retries, proxy calls backend with `Resume-Start: v1|sid|offset|hmac` and backend replies `Resume-Ack: v1|ok|offset` or `Resume-Nack: v1|reason`. keep messages small and deterministic.
sam.w: security: trailer blobs must be HMAC-signed. if teams need confidentiality, offer optional envelope encryption via KMS per-route. KMS adds cross-region complexity and a degrade path (kms->hmac) decision.
maria: propose defaults: HMAC-only for most routes; encryption opt-in for regulated tenants. add route config `stream.resume = { mode: trailers|header_fallback|off, retention_s: int, kms_required: bool }`. default mode `trailers|header_fallback` for generative streams.
ingrid: implementation notes for proxies: 1) do not buffer whole stream to get trailer; stream-forward and capture trailer when it arrives, 2) if proxy cannot forward trailers, write trailer blob to local encrypted store with TTL from route config, 3) proxies must validate HMAC before allowing resume. drop invalid headers and emit metric `resume.hmac.invalid`.
kai: for header fallback, keep `X-RW-META` tiny (<=1kb). prefer trailer for big state. header fallback should ONLY carry a reference (sid) + small attempt counter, not full checkpoint.
sam.w: operational concerns: key rotation, KMS availability, and a fast kill-switch to disable resume if resume infra misbehaves. need metrics: resume.attempts, resume.success, resume.latency.p50/p95, resume.store_hits, resume.store_misses, resume.hmac_invalid.
maria: storage TTL guidance: short-lived checkpoints: default 60s for interactive streams, 300s for long-running batch generative jobs. route owners can tune. store must encrypt-at-rest and delete on TTL.
ingrid: dedupe: backend provides `Resume-Ack` with a `dedupe_token` when it can safely dedupe. proxies should not auto-retry for side-effecting routes unless `dedupe_mode=strict` on route config. default dedupe_mode=off for side-effects.
kai: avoid retry amplification: add per-route retry budget and an origin tag in resume handshake (`origin=client|edge`). proxies only consume edge budget for edge-origin retries. include `origin_attempts` in token so we can limit total attempts.
sam.w: client guidance: clients must include `should_resume=true|false`. if false, edge must not auto-resume on disconnect to avoid duplicate side-effects. recommend exponential backoff and jitter for client retries.
maria: migration: canary region with trailer support enabled, edge-store disabled. next enable edge-store in fallback regions, then enable header-fallback for legacy SDKs. document compatibility matrix.
ingrid: corner cases: what if a proxy writes trailer to store but crashes before metadata propagation? ensure backend can NACK with `stale_checkpoint` and client falls back to fresh restart. also consider partial-stream checkpoints; resume offset semantics must be explicit (byte offset vs chunk id).
kai: good point. define checkpoint proto: {resume_id, last_chunk_index, last_token_index, model_state_hint}. keep it minimal. trailers carry utf8 base64(proto) + hmac prefix: `v1|hmac|payload`.
sam.w: ops-bot: please create rollout checklist and a canary playbook. include key-rotation steps and KMS fail-mode options.
ops-bot: created RW-6012: "streaming-resume-trailer-vs-header rollout" and pinged #eng-oncall.
maria: final ask: include a small example flow in the RFC showing timeline for resume under 200ms added median latency. kai: can you add that?
kai: will do  i'll draft RFC with handshake state machine, checkpoint proto example, proxy implementation checklist, route knobs, key-policy options (hmac vs kms), metrics, and migration plan. tagging infra/ops/security for review.
